assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is one of the most consequential translational stories in modern medicine: a clear mechanistic discovery (proglucagon-derived GLP-1 as an incretin and satiety signal) that led to durable treatments for type 2 diabetes and obesity with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are all exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its insulinotropic action) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor signaling, therapeutic translation) are the clearest scientific anchors; Mojsov's contribution to identifying and synthesizing the active peptide form is real but credit is debated and I cannot independently adjudicate it. Knudsen's pharmaceutical engineering is important but is drug development more than discovery, and Habener-type contributors are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, large randomized outcome trials and mass clinical use make the work mature; timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener-lineage work (not on this list), Holst, Drucker and Knudsen is contested.
I am recalling trial and history details from memory and have not verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of intracellular signaling from the ER to the nucleus, an original and conceptually clean discovery with broad relevance to secretory physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and immunity.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter, with complementary yeast genetic and biochemical work (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing), form a natural and widely accepted pair; Mori and Walter together capture the pathway's decisive steps. Other contributors (e.g. Ron, Harding on PERK/ATF6 branches) are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of confirmation across species; the core pathway is stable. Therapeutic payoff is still emerging, which weighs against it only modestly for a basic-science prize.
uncertainties: Whether additional branches (PERK/ATF6) would be expected in the credit is not resolved by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, a genuine paradigm shift in cancer therapy bridging basic immunology and cell engineering. Impact is major and clinically proven.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CD28-containing receptors, design principles), June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL/ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials) form a plausible trio; Eshhar and others who made first-generation CARs are not on this list, so the configuration may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Approved products, multi-year follow-up and independent replication exist; toxicity and solid-tumor limits remain, but recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Foundational CAR originators outside the credited list may be seen as omitted.
Long-term durability and safety data continue to accrue.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and the demonstration that its blockade produces clinical benefit transformed rheumatology and inflammatory bowel disease treatment. A clear, proven concept-to-therapy path with enormous patient impact.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly made the decisive cellular and clinical proof-of-concept; they are a tight, widely recognized pair. Contributions of the cytokine biology and antibody-engineering community are acknowledged but not credited here. I note my field of rheumatology, so I weigh this strictly on the common criteria.
assessment.maturity: Biologic anti-TNF therapy has been standard care for over two decades with extensive confirmation; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer recognizing the cytokine biology or the therapeutic translation is open.
Antibody engineering contributors are outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a general tool for causal, cell-type-specific control of activity, and has reshaped the study of circuits, behavior and, increasingly, therapy (e.g. vision restoration). Originality and methodological impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: The channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Bamberg, Hegemann) and the neuronal implementation and circuit application (Boyden, Deisseroth; Miesenböck's earlier genetic photostimulation) make this a difficult six-person allocation. A trio of Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth is plausible but excludes Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for more than a decade; the tool is mature, though human therapeutic validation is limited.
uncertainties: Credit is split between discovery of the opsin and its neuronal use, and cannot cleanly fit three names.
Whether a tool/method counts as physiological discovery is a committee judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR signaling established how cells couple nutrient and growth-factor signals to growth and metabolism, with implications for cancer, diabetes, ageing and transplantation (rapamycin). A foundational and highly cited discovery.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and defined its role in growth control; Schreiber's chemical biology of rapamycin-FKBP12 and identification of the target were pivotal. Sabatini's mTORC1 mechanistic work is substantial, but I would hesitate over inclusion; I cannot resolve that fully.
assessment.maturity: Core findings are confirmed in multiple systems; clinical exploitation (rapalogs) is real but modest compared with the basic impact.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and others (e.g. Brown, Heitman, Hall-era yeast work) is uncertain.
Some facts on priority are from memory and unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition defined the model of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, turning CML from a fatal into a chronically managed disease. Clear, original and of lasting influence.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (clinical proof and development) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio; the Rowley and Witte/Baltimore discoveries of the underlying genetics are outside the supplied names and may be relevant to a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of outcome data and independent confirmation; recognition is mature, though its Lasker recognition suggests it has been well celebrated already.
uncertainties: Whether the underlying oncogene discovery (not credited here) should be part of any recognition.
Drug development may weigh less than discovery science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning and characterization of IL-6 and the later clinical blockade of its receptor (tocilizumab) revealed a central inflammatory cytokine with relevance to rheumatoid arthritis, Castleman disease, cytokine release syndrome and COVID-19.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano did the decisive cytokine identification and cloning; credit for therapeutic antibody engineering is distributed to industry scientists not listed. The pair is clean and coherent.
assessment.maturity: Therapy is established and the biology confirmed broadly; recognition is timely though somewhat overshadowed by TNF-blockade precedence.
uncertainties: Relative weight of basic discovery versus therapeutic blockade.
Overlap with an anti-TNF candidate in the same therapeutic space.
